archetype: Naya Dinosaur typal battlecruiser: a linear critical-mass ramp deck whose headline payoff is one {5}{R}{G}{W} commander's combat-damage trigger, carrying a five-card enrage converter set as its combat-independent second engine, an ignition layer of exactly two cards that can make that commander cheaper, and a bracket-report floor of 4 whose verified reality argues 3.

role_assignment.default_role: Quiet ramp player through the first six turns — a control POSTURE, not a control deck (strategy:whos-the-beatdown). The posture only earns its keep if the deflection turns are also development turns: ramp/fixing is drawn by turn 6 in 86.9% of goldfish games at mean turn 2.044, and mean available mana is 5.486 at turn 6. What the posture cannot promise is a mid-game value line, because the enrage web is a CONJUNCTION — the five converters land by turn 6 in 50.6% of games, and they convert nothing until a damage source is also on the board (strategy:mulligans.engine-hands: payoffs without the enabler are blanks). Experienced tables will discount the posture, and be right to.
role_assignment.pivot_trigger: Castable commander plus a held board-wide protection instant plus an opponent who cannot profitably block or answer (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window). One caveat the protection count hides: of the five protection spells, only Flawless Maneuver is castable for nothing on the turn you tap out for an eight-drop. The alternative pivot is engine-side and cheaper: Forerunner of the Empire plus any one enrage converter restarts at two cards, against 8 plus {2} per prior command-zone cast (strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance).

engines.engine: Engine one, VERIFIED: combat damage to a player reveals that many cards and free-rolls every Dinosaur among them onto the battlefield. Stack 001 (checker pass) resolves the cascade on a real board — one 7-damage connection into five new bodies, three Garruk's Uprising draws and a Pantlaza discover at X=6 — with the sequencing lesson that Pantlaza's once-per-turn discover must resolve BEFORE the Regisaur Alpha token enters. The reveal is dense by construction: 29 of the deck's 34 creature copies are Dinosaurs (cards.json type lines), the five that are not being Huatli, Intrepid Paleontologist, Otepec Huntmaster, Selvala and Forerunner of the Empire — so the trigger never free-rolls the web's own damage source.
engines.evidence: verified stack 001 (checker pass); cards.json type lines (34 creature copies, 29 Dinosaur); deck-facts roles (threat:body 34)

engines.engine: THE BINDING AXIS. A command-zone cast can only be made cheaper by a cost reducer, and exactly two maindeck cards do it: Otepec Huntmaster ('Dinosaur spells you cast cost {1} less') and Urza's Incubator ('Creature spells of the chosen type cost {2} less'). The 'Cost reducer or cheat-into-play drawn' target measures six cards at 67.3% assembled, 56.2% by turn 6 — but Descendants' Path casts off the top of the library, Belbe's Portal and Monster Manual put a creature from HAND onto the battlefield, and Huatli's Roar chapter III searches a Dinosaur to hand. None of those four can reach the command zone. Two named cards is 13.7% of an opening seven by the same hypergeometric that gives strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors its 7.1% for one. Against that: goldfish mean cast turn 7.969, median 8, 8.3% by turn 6, and 5,533 of 10,000 iterations never cast him by turn 10 — a conservative bound, since the simulation models no cost reduction at all.
engines.evidence: goldfish_metrics.json (mean_cast_turn 7.969, cast_by_turn_6_rate 0.083, cast_turn_histogram not_by_max_turn 5533, targets); deck-audit engine components; oracle text (cards.json)

engines.engine: The web's damage source, and the deck's only free repeatable one. 'Whenever a Dinosaur you control enters, you may have this creature deal 1 damage to each creature' — one optional ping per Dinosaur entry, no mana, no combat step. Six maindeck cards can damage your own Dinosaurs (Forerunner, Zacama, Blasphemous Act, Itzquinth, Triumphant Chomp, Trumpeting Carnosaur); four are one-shots and Zacama's costs {2}{R} a shot off a nine-mana body. No goldfish target measures a converter and a source TOGETHER, so the rate that would describe the web actually running has never been simulated. Its ETB also stacks the top card: search a Dinosaur, reveal, shuffle, put it on top — which is the commander's reveal, pre-loaded.
engines.evidence: oracle text (cards.json); verified stacks 003 and 005 (checker pass, both ignited by this card); goldfish_targets.json declares no source-plus-converter target

engines.piece: Enrage converters (Ripjaw Raptor, Polyraptor, Ranging Raptors, Trapjaw Tyrant, Wrathful Raptors)
engines.engine: Engine two, VERIFIED: the five cards that turn damage on your own board into something. Stack 005 (checker pass) resolves one optional Forerunner ping and banks five payoffs — an opponent's 1/1 dead to state-based actions, their 3/3 exiled under Trapjaw Tyrant, a Ripjaw draw, a tapped basic Forest off Ranging Raptors, and a Polyraptor copy token whose own entry re-arms Forerunner with a genuinely new optional trigger. Cost: 1 damage marked on each of your six creatures, all surviving, clearing at cleanup. Goldfish: 60.8% assembled, 50.6% by turn 6, mean turn 3.053 — a five-card class, which strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors prices at 31% of openers. Wrathful Raptors is the fifth converter and the one that converts damage into reach rather than cards: 'Whenever a Dinosaur you control is dealt damage, it deals that much damage to any target that isn't a Dinosaur.'
engines.evidence: verified stack 005 (checker pass); goldfish_metrics.json ('Enrage engine drawn' 0.608 assembled / 0.506 by t6 / mean turn 3.053); deck-audit engine component (size 5, opening_seven 0.312); oracle text

engines.piece: Blasphemous Act + Temple Altisaur (the one-sided sweep)
engines.engine: VERIFIED, and the sharpest single card-pair in the deck. Temple Altisaur is a prevention shield, not an enrage payoff: 'If a source would deal damage to ANOTHER Dinosaur you control, prevent all but 1 of that damage' — it is what makes a 13-point sweeper one-sided. Stack 004 (checker pass) resolves the whole line with the checker's correction of scale: Altisaur is not 'another Dinosaur' to itself, eats the unprevented 13 and dies, while your other Dinosaurs are each dealt exactly 1 and survive; state-based actions clear the opponents' creatures BEFORE Wrathful Raptors' redirect targets are chosen, so all 16 redirect damage (13 from Altisaur via last known information, plus 1 each from three survivors) can only go at a player — 26 to 10, not lethal. Ripjaw draws. The Act itself costs {R} off nine creatures. What the line costs is drawing both halves: 2.5% assembled, 1.4% by turn 6, mean turn 5.462, because each half is a single named card at 7.1% of an opening seven. This is a real answer to a go-wide table and a real reason to keep both cards, not a plan.
engines.evidence: verified stack 004 (checker pass); goldfish_metrics.json ('THE ONE-SIDED APOCALYPSE' 0.025 assembled / 0.014 by t6 / mean turn 5.462); deck-audit single_points_of_failure (component size 1, opening_seven 0.071); oracle text

engines.piece: Polyraptor + Forerunner of the Empire (the bounded burst)
engines.engine: VERIFIED BOUNDED, and the crux of the bracket conversation. The combo DB tags this pairing a two-card infinite at mana_value_needed 0, and that tag alone drives the computed floor to 4 (bracket_report.json driver 'two_card_infinite'). Stack 003 (checker pass) resolved the actual ceiling: a maximum of SEVEN Polyraptor tokens, reached only by DECLINING one intermediate 'you may' trigger — saying yes to everything caps at six — self-terminating when Forerunner dies to its own third sweep, and safely stoppable at every link. The load-bearing word is 'may'. Stack 002 (checker pass) resolves the same copy loop beside a MANDATORY pinger (Marauding Raptor, a card this deck does not run) and finds no exit at all: every trigger is forced, 2 damage never kills a fresh 5/5 token, and CR 732.4 / 104.4b end the game in a draw unless an opponent breaks it on their terms.
engines.evidence: verified stack 003 (checker pass); verified stack 002 (checker pass); bracket_report.json drivers and two_card_infinites; deck-facts combos (1 contained line, 1 two-card infinite)

engines.engine: Once-per-turn discover X equal to the entering Dinosaur's toughness — no combat step and no eight mana required, which makes it the payoff that keeps working on the turn after a sweeper (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math). Verified in situ by stack 001, including the once-per-turn sequencing trap: stack the discover to resolve before the Regisaur Alpha token enters or lose the large X. It sits inside the seven-card 'Dinosaur payoff' group the simulation measures at 73.7% assembled, 62.3% by turn 6 — a group whose members are not interchangeable: only Pantlaza and Forerunner trigger on EACH Dinosaur entering, Curious Altisaur and Quartzwood Crasher want combat damage to a player, and Garruk's Uprising wants power 4 or greater.
engines.evidence: verified stack 001 (checker pass); goldfish_metrics.json ('Dinosaur payoff drawn' 0.737 / 0.623 by t6); oracle text

engines.piece: Big-mana acceleration (Selvala, Heart of the Wilds + Regal Behemoth)
engines.engine: The direct attack on a 7.969 mean cast turn: Selvala taps for X equal to the greatest power among your creatures, which the deck's 5/5s make 5 or more from the mid-game; Regal Behemoth grants the monarch and adds an extra mana on every land tap while you hold the crown. goldfish_metrics.json's stated assumptions exclude cost reducers, rituals and extra draw, so 7.969 is the floor of the problem rather than the expectation — but any acceleration claim here is projection, not simulation, and should be labelled that way. Monarch carries its own cost: the crown paints its holder (strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection).

engines.piece: Ramp shell (35 land copies over 24 entries + 6 ramp:land + 5 rocks + 3 dorks + 3 cost-reduction)
engines.engine: 48 mana sources against Burgess' 42 (31 + 3 colours + a mana value 8 commander) clears the yardstick by six, 13 of them persistent nonland producers; the 35 land copies sit one under the 36-38 template. The strain is colour, not quantity: land sources run G20/R16/W14, which the rocks and dorks lift to totals of G26/R20/W20 against a Karsten 90% yardstick of 36 apiece, and mana_analysis puts the on-curve rate with rocks and dorks at W 0.58, R 0.58, G 0.742. Wakening Sun's Avatar wants WWW and Austere Command and Trapjaw Tyrant want WW off 20 white. 12 of 35 lands enter tapped (34%), 7 of them unconditionally, against the roughly eight taplands strategy:deckbuilding.mana-base calls comfortable in a slow deck. Two mana traps deck-facts names: Unclaimed Territory is spells-only and cannot activate Belbe's Portal or Monster Manual, while Secluded Courtyard's clause explicitly says 'or activate an ability' and does pay those costs. Consistency is genuinely good — 89.4% of games make the turn-3 land drop and 77.1% of first sevens are keepable — but the land-drop rate falls to 52.6% by turn 6 and the deck then rides rocks and dorks, exactly the profile a sweeper punishes on board and mana at once.
engines.evidence: deck-audit axes (mana-sources 48 vs 42, mana-base 35, taplands 7, colour-sources -16, consistency 0.894); mana_analysis.json (sources, on_curve_probability, enters_tapped 12/35); goldfish_metrics.json (land_drop_hit_rate t3 0.894 / t6 0.526, mean_available_mana t6 5.486, keep_first_seven_rate 0.771); deck-facts notes on restricted mana

engines.piece: Protection suite (Akroma's Will, Heroic Intervention, Flawless Maneuver, Boros Charm, Eerie Interlude)
engines.engine: Six protection copies by role, inside the 5-7 band, and the lowest-measured declared group in the deck: 59.0% assembled, 48.5% by turn 6. Read the five rather than counting them. Heroic Intervention's hexproof and Akroma's Will's protection from each colour answer targeted exile and bounce, so the group is broader than indestructible; Eerie Interlude is the only member that dodges a non-targeted mass exile; and Flawless Maneuver is the only one castable for nothing, which matters because on the turn you tap out for an eight-drop it is the only one you can cast. A second duty: the board-wide instants are the only shields that cover Forerunner of the Empire, which stands outside every tribal protection layer in the deck.
engines.evidence: deck-audit axis protection (6 copies, target 5-7); goldfish_metrics.json ('Protection held for the board' 0.590 / 0.485 by t6); oracle text

engines.piece: Card advantage (Garruk's Uprising, Curious Altisaur, Bonehoard Dracosaur, Etali, Ripjaw Raptor, Selvala + eight the taxonomy does not tag)
engines.engine: The cheapest rebuild package after a sweeper (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math), and an axis whose count is a floor rather than a hole. deck-audit reads 6 copies against a template of 10 and attaches its own probe note naming Jetmir's Garden, Rishkar's Expertise and Vaultborn Tyrant; reading oracle text across all 89 entries adds Descendants' Path, Hunter's Insight, Pantlaza, Regal Behemoth's monarch and Trumpeting Carnosaur's discover 5 as well. Three of those — Descendants' Path, Hunter's Insight, Rishkar's Expertise — have no entry in card_roles.json at all, which is why the axis under-reads. Ripjaw Raptor's enrage draw is verified live in stacks 004 and 005: with a damage source down, drawing cards is a side effect of every ping.
engines.evidence: deck-audit axis card-advantage (6 copies, probe note); deck-facts roles (draw:engine 4, draw:impulse 2, no_role list); verified stacks 004 and 005; oracle text

engines.piece: Interaction suite (11 removal copies inside an 18-card interactive suite)
engines.engine: The least typal thing about the deck and its best-built axis: 11 removal pieces against Walser's 8-10 baseline, 2 sweepers inside the 1-3 band, and all five permanent classes answered with nothing uncovered. Two of those classes rest on one card each — Intrepid Paleontologist for graveyard, Beast Within for land — which makes them the fragile coverage rather than surplus. Eleven tutors, all tagged narrow, and seven of them fetch lands; Congregation at Dawn is the exception the taxonomy files as a tutor and the deck uses as an engine piece, since stacking three Dinosaur creature cards on top at instant speed IS the commander's reveal.
engines.evidence: deck-audit axes (interaction 11, interactive_suite_copies 18, sweepers 2, interaction-breadth 5 with uncovered []); deck-facts roles (removal:spot 6, removal:damage 5, removal:sweeper 2, tutor:narrow 11); oracle text

candidate_missing_lines.title: One Forerunner ping with Wrathful Raptors on the board: how much reach is a single Dinosaur entry worth?
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: All five are in the 99, and the two checker-passed boards that would answer this never overlap: stack 005's ping web resolves with no Wrathful Raptors out, and stack 004's Wrathful redirects come off Blasphemous Act with no Forerunner in play. Wrathful Raptors reads 'Whenever a Dinosaur you control is dealt damage, it deals that much damage to any target that isn't a Dinosaur', and stack 004 establishes that a prevented-down-to-1 hit still deals 1 and still fires a redirect. So a single free ping across N of your Dinosaurs plausibly throws N damage at a player while ALSO paying every enrage converter — and Forerunner itself, a Human Soldier, is not a Dinosaur, so its own self-damage should fire nothing. The trigger count, the ordering against state-based actions, and whether the redirect can be pointed at a planeswalker or a player freely need resolving before any number goes in print.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Temple Altisaur under someone else's damage-based sweeper
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Temple Altisaur's prevention names no source: 'If a source would deal damage to another Dinosaur you control, prevent all but 1 of that damage.' Stack 004 verifies it against the deck's own Blasphemous Act. If it reads the same way against an opponent's damage-based wipe, the deck's single worst matchup — a mid-game sweeper on a committed board — has a two-mana-cheaper answer than any protection instant it runs, and the enrage converters turn that wipe into draws, ramp and exile instead. The scope is narrow and worth bounding: it does nothing against destroy, exile, sacrifice or -X/-X effects, and Altisaur itself is unprotected. Nothing in the artifact set resolves the opposing-source case.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Selvala or Regal Behemoth into an early commander cast
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Selvala taps for X equal to the greatest power among your creatures, which the deck's 5/5s make 5 or more; Regal Behemoth adds a mana on every land tap while you are the monarch. goldfish_metrics.json's stated assumptions exclude neither card by name but do exclude cost reducers and rituals, and its 7.969 mean cast turn is measured without any acceleration model beyond rocks and lands. No artifact quantifies how many turns these two actually buy, so the claim needs either a goldfish model extension or a worked sequencing scenario before a number is stated anywhere.

matchup_frames.vs_sweeper_control: The worst frame, with one narrow consolation. 'Deploy in waves' (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math) is structurally unavailable when the commander's trigger IS the wave, and a wipe takes the acceleration layer with the board — 5 rocks, 3 dorks, Selvala and Regal Behemoth — which is exactly why mean available mana is 5.486 at turn 6 and 7.321 at turn 10. Swing only with a board-wide protection instant held, into the tapped-out turn (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window). The consolation is a rebuild ordering, not a shield: Forerunner plus any one converter restarts the value engine at two cards, against 8 plus {2} per prior command-zone cast for the other plan (strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance) — and Ranging Raptors' lands and Ripjaw's draws are banked where Trapjaw's exile is not, since the hostage returns when Trapjaw leaves.
matchup_frames.vs_stax: Taxes hit an eight-drop hardest, so fight over enablers rather than payoffs (strategy:critical-mass) and mulligan toward the ignition layer, not the payoffs (strategy:mulligans.engine-hands) — remembering it is a two-card class at 13.7% of openers, so the honest mulligan target is 'a mana engine plus a Dinosaur', not a named card. Forerunner's web is the best under-stax posture in the deck: it runs on creature entries rather than activations or big casts, and Selvala's single activation makes big mana tax-resilient. Spend the 11 removal pieces on whatever turns off mana or creature entry specifically (strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy), and note that Unclaimed Territory cannot activate Belbe's Portal or Monster Manual.
matchup_frames.vs_aggro: The deck owns the long game (strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock) and should take the control role. Two verified catch-up plays back that, at very different frequencies: Trapjaw Tyrant plus one Forerunner ping is repeatable exile removal for the one creature that actually races (stack 005), available whenever the web is up; Blasphemous Act through Temple Altisaur is a board-clearing 16-damage redirect (stack 004) that assembles in 2.5% of games. Plan around the first and be delighted by the second. Turn the corner immediately on stabilising (strategy:combat-math.racing) — mean bodies is 2.706 at turn 6, so the board that survives is small and needs the trigger or the ping to grow.
matchup_frames.vs_combo: The bad seat: no counterspells in Naya, 11 spot answers and 2 sweepers, and a clock that starts when an eight-drop resolves at a median turn 8. Per strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy, spend removal on enablers now rather than banking it for a payoff that may never be answerable, and take the beatdown role regardless of posture (strategy:whos-the-beatdown). The web speeds the clock at the margin — tokens, exile on their blockers, Wrathful reach — but contributes zero pieces of interaction. The honest plan is racing, and the honest mulligan is toward ramp and a cheap threat rather than toward the commander.

distribution_notes: 65 nonland entries over 35 land copies (24 land entries, 89 entries, 100 copies). Curve by nonland entry: 6 at one, 9 at two, 18 at three, 8 at four, 10 at five, 6 at six, 2 at seven, 3 at eight, 2 at nine and one at twelve — modal mana value 3, but six entries at mana value 8+ against the roughly 1.5 strategy:deckbuilding.curve measures in an average Commander deck, and the deck's headline plan is one of the six. Roughly half the deck makes or reduces mana beneath a 34-body typal top, of which 29 copies are Dinosaurs. Goldfish (10,000 iterations, seed 42, decklist sha 0480aaf7d19e): ramp/fixing 93.9% assembled and 86.9% by turn 6 at mean turn 2.044; Dinosaur payoff 73.7%/62.3%; cost reducer or cheat 67.3%/56.2%; connection kit 62.2%/51.4%; enrage converters 60.8%/50.6% at mean turn 3.053; protection 59.0%/48.5%; the Blasphemous Act plus Temple Altisaur sweep 2.5%/1.4% at mean turn 5.462. Commander mean cast 7.969, median 8, 8.3% by turn 6, never cast by turn 10 in 5,533 of 10,000 iterations — with cost reduction unmodeled, so that is a conservative bound. Land-drop hit rate 89.4% at turn 3 and 52.6% at turn 6; mean available mana 5.486 at turn 6; mean bodies 2.706 at turn 6; 77.1% of first sevens keepable at 0.28 mean mulligans. Pips: G 54 across 38 cards, W 23 across 18, R 19 across 15, against a 36-source yardstick per colour that a 35-land deck cannot reach. Land sources G20/R16/W14 lift to totals of G26/R20/W20 through 5 rocks and 3 dorks, putting the on-curve rate at W 0.58, R 0.58, G 0.742. Role coverage 94.4%; the five cards the taxonomy has no pattern for — Descendants' Path, Hunter's Insight, Overwhelming Stampede, Rishkar's Expertise, Triumphant Chomp — are functional slots, not dead ones, and three of them are card advantage the axis cannot see. synergy_graph.json has 77 edges falling inside this deck, which is a top-10 global shortlist landing here often, not a per-deck fit score.
key_tensions: IGNITION IS THE AXIS THAT BINDS. Engine one is entirely a commander combat trigger; the commander costs {5}{R}{G}{W}; and exactly two maindeck cards — Otepec Huntmaster and Urza's Incubator — can make a command-zone cast cheaper, a 13.7% opening-seven class. Goldfish measures the consequence at mean cast turn 7.969, median 8, 8.3% by turn 6, with 5,533 of 10,000 games never casting him by turn 10, while strategy:deckbuilding.curve warns that in a 7-10 turn format 'you're probably only going to be able to cast ONE big-mana spell per game'. The 67.3% attached to the cost-reducer-or-cheat group is a real number about a group that mostly does something else: four of its six members move cards from hand or library, and none of the four can touch the command zone. Every recast adds {2} on top (strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance).

THE WEB IS A CONJUNCTION AND NOTHING MEASURES THE CONJUNCTION. The five enrage converters — Ripjaw Raptor, Polyraptor, Ranging Raptors, Trapjaw Tyrant, Wrathful Raptors — assemble at 60.8%, 50.6% by turn 6. They convert nothing without damage, and Forerunner of the Empire is the only free repeatable source in the 99; the other five self-damage cards are one-shots or cost {2}{R} off a nine-mana body. goldfish_targets.json declares no target pairing a converter with a source, so the rate at which the web actually RUNS has never been simulated — the two classes are 31.2% and 36.4% of openers separately and the product is what the deck lives on (strategy:mulligans.engine-hands: 'Payoffs without the enabler are blanks until the engine exists').

THE WEB HANGS ON A HUMAN. Every checker-passed ping line in this deck is ignited by Forerunner of the Empire, a 1/3 Human Soldier standing outside every tribal layer the deck owns: Temple Altisaur's prevention names other DINOSAURS, Secluded Courtyard and Unclaimed Territory name Dinosaurs, the commander's reveal free-rolls only Dinosaurs, Descendants' Path misses it, and its own sweep damages it — 1 of 3 in stack 005, dead to its own third sweep in stack 003. Only the board-wide protection instants (48.5% held by turn 6) cover it, and opponents who read the board kill a 1/3 first and cheaply (strategy:threat-assessment).

THE FLOOR CONVERSATION: the report computes 4, the verified record argues 3. bracket_report.json's floor is 4 on a single driver — the combo DB tags Polyraptor plus Forerunner a two-card infinite at mana_value_needed 0 — while its other two drivers (two Game Changers, combo content) force only 3. Stack 003 (checker pass) resolved that pairing as BOUNDED: a maximum of seven tokens, reachable only by declining an intermediate trigger, self-terminating when Forerunner dies to its own third sweep, stoppable at every link. The bracket engine does not consult passing stacks. Present the report's 4 and open Rule 0 with the verified fact, exactly as strategy:deckbuilding.power-level frames it — contents give a floor, never a verdict, and brackets are a tool for the pregame conversation. That conversation is the system working (strategy:deckbuilding.power-level.barometers).

SWEEPER EXPOSURE RUNS THROUGH THE MANA, NOT THE LANDS. 35 land copies is an ordinary count and the 6 land-ramp spells bank their mana on the wrath-proof side of the table. What a wipe takes is everything above it: 5 rocks to an artifact sweep, 3 dorks plus Selvala and Regal Behemoth to any board wipe, and mean available mana is 5.486 at turn 6 precisely because the deck rides that layer after the land-drop rate falls to 52.6%. The one asymmetry the deck owns is Temple Altisaur's damage floor, verified against its own Blasphemous Act (stack 004) and unverified against anyone else's sweeper.
overall_assessment: This is a fair battlecruiser with a verified second engine and one expensive ignition. The deck plays the critical-mass game (strategy:critical-mass): six or seven turns of deflection-postured ramp (strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection) into a pivot (strategy:pivot-point, strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window) that costs {5}{R}{G}{W} and that exactly two cards in the 99 can discount — which is why goldfish puts the mean cast turn at 7.969 and why the binding constraint is ignition rather than payoff density. Alongside it runs a checker-verified enrage web: with Forerunner of the Empire down, one optional ping converts any Dinosaur entry into exile-removal, ramp, a card and a fresh 5/5 that re-arms the trigger (stack 005), with a bounded seven-token burst mode (stack 003) and a one-sided table sweep through Temple Altisaur's damage floor (stack 004) beside it. The honest correction to that optimism is arithmetic: the web is a conjunction of five converters at 60.8% and a damage class whose only free repeatable member is a 1/3 Human outside all tribal protection, and no simulation prices the two together. Its interaction is genuinely good for a linear typal list — 11 removal pieces, all five permanent classes covered — and its bracket story is a conversation the deck should have out loud: the report computes 4 off a DB tag that a checker-passed stack bounded at seven tokens. Two structural weaknesses stand: the pivot is late and thinly discounted, and the value engine's ignition is a single fragile body.
gaps: No section on typal/tribal construction: critical mass of a creature type, typal-land tradeoffs, and the off-tribe hub creature that every tribal protection layer ignores. This deck needed it at four points.

No section on self-damage engines — damage to your own permanents as a resource. The nearest hits are life-total sections. This deck has a verified such engine and no doctrine to cite for piloting it.

Load-bearing: no arithmetic for CONJUNCTIONS. strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors prices one effect class at a time (5 copies is 31% of openers, 7 is 41%), but an engine needing class A AND class B together — a converter and a damage source, a sweeper and its prevention shield — has no treatment anywhere in the doc, and it is exactly where this deck's two rate figures mislead.

No section distinguishing cost REDUCTION from cheat-into-play. They are the same shelf in most articles and different cards for a commander deck: only a reducer touches a command-zone cast, and a deck can measure 67.3% on a group of six while holding two cards that matter.
No section on top-of-library stacking as setup discipline — Congregation at Dawn or Worldly Tutor into a reveal trigger, and Forerunner's own search-and-stack ETB.

No section on reconciling a computed bracket signal with a checker-passed stack that bounds it: when the DB tag and the verified line disagree, what does the pregame conversation owe the table? strategy:deckbuilding.power-level gestures at it, but the verified-refutation case deserves its own treatment.
